instructions:
The principal wants a yes/no answer. Using ONLY the listed fields (refer to each as
latest("<ref>")), write a decision rule as a boolean expression with explicit thresholds, the conventional or
physical reason for each threshold, and short labels for yes and no. The rationale must hold on any day: do not
mention today's values in it. If an existing service already gives a
direct verdict or index, you may use it, but prefer rules that remain correct if one source is missing (use 'or' /
'and' deliberately). A field that holds several numbers (e.g. hourly values "30 20 10 0") can be given to max(),
min() or sum(), e.g. max(latest("src:field")) >= 50. Allowed functions: latest, max, min, sum, round, coalesce,
if_else, max_over, min_over. Do not invent fields. One or two rules at most.

exclude: Overnight and evening hours outside the drying period
Forecasts for other days or other cities
questions.quantity: Verdict on whether outdoor line-drying today in Osaka is suitable, based on forecast conditions over the daytime drying period: chance/amount of precipitation, humidity, wind, temperature/sunshine. Verdict plus the key reasons.
questions.question: Is today a good day to dry laundry outside in Osaka?
questions.population: Osaka city, today's daytime hours (local time, roughly 08:00-18:00)

fields.value_now: 北の風　海上　では　北の風　やや強く
fields.meaning: Forecast wind direction and qualitative strength text for the prefecture and sea areas; no numeric speed

expr.description: boolean expression using latest("ref") over the given refs, comparisons, and/or/not, numbers

rules.question: Is today a good day to dry laundry outside in Osaka (wind-only check; rain, humidity and sun are unknown)?
rules.yes_label: Yes: wind forecast gives no blocking sign (rain/humidity not verifiable)
rules.no_label: No/unknown: wind forecast missing, cannot support a verdict
rules.rationale: The only permitted field is a qualitative JMA wind text with no numeric speed, and it carries no precipitation, humidity, temperature or sunshine information. It can only show that a forecast exists. Moderate wind helps drying, and a strong or very strong wind wording would be a reason to say no (laundry blows off the line), but the allowed functions cannot parse that text reliably. This verdict is therefore weak. A real answer needs precipitation probability and humidity fields, which were not provided.

thresholds.why: Wind text is qualitative with no numeric speed. Presence is the only testable condition, and 'strong wind' wording would be the conventional reason to avoid line-drying.
